newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo's Remeron outperforms in trials.
newsitem.headline: Akzo's Remeron outperforms in trials.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Wednesday that results of clinical and everyday trials with its new anti-depressant Remeron showed it to be more effective than existing so-called SSRI drugs such as Prozac.

Study results unveiled during 6th World Congress of Biological Psychiatry currently being held in Nice, France, showed Remeron was more effective than fluoxetine (Prozac) in treating depression, Akzo's pharmaceuticals arm Organon said.
It was also shown to be superior to TCA amitriptyline in preventing relapses during long-term treatment, while side-effects were shown to be minimal in practice, it said.

"Full results of the Remeron-fluoxetine study...show that at weeks three and four, patients treated with Remeron were significantly less depressed than those taking fluoxetine," it said, adding "This trend continued to the end of the study."

It said results of the study, the first direct comparison of Remeron and a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant had been presented in Nice by Professor David Nutt of Bristol University's Psychopharmacology unit.
In the relapse prevention study conducted by London's St Mary's Hospital Medical School, eight percent of Remeron treated patients relapsed in the long term.
This compared with 22 percent of patients receiving amitriptyline, the study found.
"This study provides clear evidence that Remeron is a superior antidepressant to amitriptyline in the long-term treatment of depression," Professor Stuart Montgomery of St Mary's told the conference.
A third study unveiled at the conference said Remeron was widely tolerated by patients.
Only 6.5 percent of some 600 patients taking part in a naturalistic study discontinued treatment because of side-effects, conference delegates heard.
